findings.evidence: The claim that different inertial frames have different stationary observer families fails for a pure spatial translation with the same time direction and basis: the curves are exactly the same maps with their spatial labels relabelled.

The clause says each pair of frames is related by exactly one transformation, but lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations states only that such parameters exist. Uniqueness follows by comparing coordinate functions, but that argument or supplier is absent.

Momentum, angular momentum, energy and conservation are used as technical notions without definitions or exact earlier suppliers. def-cm01-units records some dimensions only, and this postulate explicitly has no dynamics or trajectories on which conservation could be defined.

The label i is an index within a model, but no cross-model identity of labels is defined. A fixed positive mass parameter within each model does not imply that every model using the same index must assign the same number. The cited particle-mass convention supports constancy per particle, not identity across model realizations.

The stated intended regime requires a classical continuum description of matter, while post-cm01-worldlines explicitly adopts discrete point-particle labels. Classical particle models do not require matter to be represented as a continuum, so this narrows the framework beyond its own particle model.

The item assigns dimensions to velocity, acceleration, the mass operator, momentum, force, energy, action and angular momentum but supplies only names and dimensions, not mathematical types and defining constructions. Its only direct dependency is def-cm-affine-time-space; the later velocity and configuration definitions are consumers of this units item.

The law uses dot x without specifying an admissible curve x:J->O, its time parameter or regularity, or an earlier derivative definition. Define a C1 curve and its derivative or formulate the allowed-velocity set directly.

findings.evidence: The symbol a denotes the spatial translation in the frame transformation and also the coordinate acceleration in a-prime=R a. Fact L1 assigns the translation components dimension length, but step 3.2 uses the acceleration dimension. The two meanings need distinct notation.

The cited sine and cosine result gives first-derivative identities, while the step concludes that R is C-infinity. Repeated differentiation does establish this and at least C2 suffices for the moving-frame supplier, but the induction is omitted.

The claim V/K isomorphic to R and dim K=3 uses a quotient/isomorphism result and rank-nullity. def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map defines kernel and image; its justified theorem thm-linear-kernel-image-and-injectivity does not prove rank-nullity. The published thm-rank-nullity gives the needed dimension formula but is absent from this item's dependencies, and no quotient-space or first-isomorphism supplier is listed.

An adapted chart requires an oriented g-orthonormal basis of K. The listed orthonormal-basis item defines the term but does not establish that such a basis exists; no finite-dimensional Gram-Schmidt or equivalent supplier is in the dependencies. The consuming frame postulate presumes such frames exist.

The remark says the group properties of both O(3) and SO(3) are proved in lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group. That lemma's statement and proof establish the properties only for SO(3); O(3) needs a separate argument or supplier.

The step uses omega-prime, but the earlier pointwise representation Omega(t)z=omega(t) cross z does not explicitly establish differentiability of t->omega(t). R in C2 makes Omega in C1 and omega's components fixed linear combinations of Omega's entries, so a short regularity argument closes the gap.
